data.narrative:
CubeFabs is a Series E semiconductor company founded by Matthew Putman (PhD, CEO; former Columbia materials science professor) alongside his father John Putman. The company operates within a fragmented competitive landscape: the Chips & Semiconductors sector contains 11 identifiable peers, comprising 3 public companies (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private firms including Cerebras, SambaNova Systems, PsiQuantum, Etched, and Tenstorrent. CubeFabs has raised approximately $182M to date.

Peer-median valuation analysis is not applicable in this instance. A same-stage cohort does not exist; only one adjacent-stage comparable was identified within the narrow semiconductor peer set, falling short of the minimum three datapoints required for statistical reliability. The full sector universe of 11 companies is too heterogeneous across stage, technology focus, and capitalization to support a credible median-based valuation without material distortion. The public comps (NVDA, AMD, ALAB) operate at different maturity and scale; private peers span multiple funding stages and business models.

Without sufficient narrow-stage comparable data, triangulation cannot be completed using the peer method. A credible valuation range for CubeFabs at Series E would require alternative methodologies—such as DCF analysis with disclosed financials, revenue multiples if available, or venture-backed precedent transactions in adjacent hardware/semiconductor rounds. The key uncertainty remains the absence of same-stage, similar-profile private transactions in this frontier sector.
